bottom_line: The ratings themselves are unchanged, but the October CPI lands at 21:30 SGT, an hour before the open, and Waller has said a hot core number puts a half-point December hike on the table. That is the worldview's top named risk, so wait for the print and the first half hour of trading before acting.
what_changed: Index futures are roughly flat (S&P +0.1% to +0.2%, Nasdaq-100 about -0.3%) after Monday's biggest S&P gain since April; no overnight shock found.
CPI is expected at +0.3% headline and +0.2% core; Waller has set +0.3% core as the level that puts 50bp on the table. This touches the 'crowded at high rates' thesis (bearish 80).
Brent fell 3.6% to below $90, the first time since August, which eases inflation worries a little.
VIX is near 20, down from 23 last week, so the rebound is calm so far; semis are still -17.5% on the month.
No after-hours earnings from AI suppliers were found for tonight; Nvidia reports Nov 17, and the Huang probe deadline is Nov 11.
